land.text: Egypt's Nubian province from the first cataract to Napata, independent 'with the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's New Kingdom row runs to -801 and overlaps this one in Nubia; the me-03 dossier should end Egyptian rule south of the first cataract c. -1070 (the page's date) or by -1000 at the latest. Kerma (2450-1450 BC) is a separate earlier polity on the page and is not a predecessor of a state founded c. 1000 BC.

land.text: Lower Nubia (Cliopatria's Nobatia shape); the Blemmyes 'in around 394 established a kingdom centered around Talmis' in its northern part

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Alodia, Makuria, Nobatia, Kingdom of Aksum, Blemmyes'. Cliopatria starts all three Nubian kingdoms in 347.

capitals.name: Napata (Jebel Barkal, Karima)
capitals.note: 'the Kushite state was centered at Napata after 1075 BC'; 'In 593 BC, it was sacked by the Egyptians and the Kushite capital was relocated to Meroë'. Coordinates 18°32′N 31°50′E from the Napata page.

capitals.name: Meroë
capitals.note: 'Aspelta moved the capital to Meroë ... possibly c. 591 BC' (Kush infobox 'Capital moved to Meroe: 591 BC'); royal burials moved fully to Meroë c. 300 BC (Kush page) or c. 270 BC (Napata page). Coordinates 16°56′N 33°43′E from the Meroë page. Napata stayed the religious centre and was restored by Natakamani after 22 BC.

keyframe_review.note: -1000 to -801, 336,379 km2: the Nile from about the first cataract (bbox 23.8 N) to the Butana. The page: 'a Kushite kingdom began to emerge around 1000 BC' centred at Napata, with no extent given, so the Lower Nubian stretch is unverified. Overlaps Cliopatria's New Kingdom of Egypt row (to -801). The infobox gives no area figure for any year.

correction.text: as drawn (Nubia, Cliopatria's Kush shape at -800). Egypt is not drawn by this dossier: the Kushite rule of Upper Egypt from c. -754, Lower Egypt from -728/-727 and the whole valley from c. -712 is the twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier's (keyframes and ledger, a constituent of Kush in hierarchy.csv); the Twenty-fifth Dynasty page: 'Shebitku conquered the entire Nile Valley, including Upper and Lower Egypt, around 712 BC'

keyframe_review.note: -800 to -701: Cliopatria's shape never leaves Nubia although the Kushites held Thebes from Kashta and Egypt from Piye; it adds Egypt only in -700. The spec is the shape at -800; fix-fx-45 (2 Nov 2026): the Egyptian gains and losses (former ledger events 1-3 and 4-11, -754 to -656) were removed because the twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier carries the same land with the same dates, and window patches m0700-m0601 reduce the -700 and -675 keyframes to Nubia. The Twenty-fifth Dynasty page disagrees on Kashta ('likely exercised some influence at Thebes' but did not control it); the Kashta page (read in the repair pass) has 'a strong degree of control over Upper Egypt'.

correction.text: the shape unchanged (Nubia with all Egypt to the Delta, 563,237 km2), for the years -727 to -671 rather than -700 to -676: Esarhaddon 'took and sacked Memphis, and Taharqa fled south' in 671

keyframe_review.note: -700 to -676: right in shape, wrong in years at both ends; the Kushite empire of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty is Cliopatria's only Egyptian keyframe for Kush. Egypt after -671 is contested with Assyria (ledger) until the sack of Thebes in -663.

correction.text: Nubia as drawn, with Upper Egypt (Thebes) still Kushite until -656: Taharqa 'reoccupied Memphis, as well as the Delta' in 669, Ashurbanipal reached Thebes in 667, Tantamani 'regained control as far north as Memphis' after 664, Thebes was sacked in 663, and 'Tantamani's authority remained recognized in Upper Egypt until 656 BCE, when Psamtik I's navy took Thebes peacefully'

keyframe_review.note: -675 to -651: Cliopatria drops Egypt entirely in -675; Lower Egypt swung between Kush and Assyria until -663 and Upper Egypt stayed Kushite to -656 (ledger). The Delta after -671 is Assyrian vassal land (Necho I at Sais), which the neo-assyrian-empire or assyrian-egypt dossier should carry.

-650 to -631: Nubia alone (336,323 km2, 56 km2 less than its neighbours: a drawing artefact). 'The last links between Kush and Upper Egypt were severed after hostilities with the Saite kings in the 590s BC'.

correction.text: the shape as drawn at -630 (Nubia to 23.8 N, Lower Nubia and the Dodekaschoinos included); the ledger takes Lower Nubia away in -274 ('In 275 or 274 BC, Ptolemy II ... sent an army to Nubia, and defeated the Kingdom of Kush'; the Triakontaschoinos 'annexed to Egypt'), returns it c. -204 ('the Kushites reasserted their control ... with Qasr Ibrim occupied'), moves the Roman border to Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa) in -22, and returns the Dodekaschoinos in 298 (Yesebokheamani after the Roman withdrawal)

keyframe_review.note: -630 to 337: one Cliopatria shape for the whole Napatan-to-Meroitic span, always reaching 23.8 N. The spec is the shape at -630; the Ptolemaic occupation the page dates only 'from the 3rd century BC', so the shape is not cut at -630. The ledger dates the Lower Nubian swings: lost -274, regained c. -204 (confidence 2), the Dodekaschoinos ceded to Rome -22, taken again in 298 (confidence 2). The capital moved to Meroë -591; Napata was sacked -593 and -22. Cliopatria's -630 keyframe matches no event on the pages.

338-346: the last shape, unchanged. 'At Meroe, the last pyramids as well as non-royal burials are dated to the mid-4th century, which is conventionally thought to be when the kingdom of Kush came to an end' (infobox 'Disestablished: c. 350 AD'); Cliopatria ends the row in 346 and starts Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia in 347. Meroë was briefly Aksumite in 330 (ledger occupation); the Meroë page says 'In 350 AD Meroë was destroyed by Axum'. The shape includes the Dodekaschoinos, which the Yesebokheamani and Dodekaschoinos pages put in Kushite hands after the Roman withdrawal of 298 (ledger), so it is kept; the reviewer's mark-adjust (minus the Dodekaschoinos after a 297 loss to the Blemmyes) rested on the earlier ledger event, which those pages do not support.

region.text: Nubia centred at Napata, from the first cataract to the Butana

ledger.note: c. 1000 BC: Kush emerges at Napata. 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC, Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata'; 'a Kushite kingdom began to emerge around 1000 BC'; the first named king, Alara, is dated 800-760 BC and the infobox gives 'Established: c. 780 BC'. The year is Cliopatria's, inside the page's range; the extent is Cliopatria's. Repair pass: the Alara page gives no reign dates and no founding date ('Alara also established Napata as the religious capital of Kush'; 'generally regarded as the founder of the Napatan royal dynasty'), so the year stays Cliopatria's at confidence 1.

c. 591 BC: the capital moves to Meroë. 'Aspelta moved the capital to Meroë ... possibly c. 591 BC' (infobox 'Capital moved to Meroe: 591 BC'), 'just after the sack of Napata by Psamtik II'; the Napata page: 'In 593 BC, it was sacked by the Egyptians and the Kushite capital was relocated to Meroë', and 'An Achaemenid raid had seriously affected Napata in 591 BC'. No border change is recorded.

region.text: the Triakontaschoinos, Lower Nubia from the first to the second cataract, 'annexed to Egypt'

ledger.note: 274 BC: Ptolemy II takes Lower Nubia. 'In 275 or 274 BC, Ptolemy II (r. 283-246 BC) sent an army to Nubia, and defeated the Kingdom of Kush'; 'Ptolemaic occupation of the far north ran from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD'. The region is the page's Triakontaschoinos read as the gazetteer's Lower Nubia.

region.text: Lower Nubia (the Triakontaschoinos): after 'there was a serious revolt at the end of the reign of Ptolemy IV, around 204 BC', 'Dynastic struggles led to the Ptolemies abandoning the area' and 'the Kushites reasserted their control ... with Qasr Ibrim occupied'

ledger.note: c. 204 BC: Kush retakes Lower Nubia. The Kush page: 'there was a serious revolt at the end of the reign of Ptolemy IV, around 204 BC'; 'Dynastic struggles led to the Ptolemies abandoning the area'; 'the Kushites reasserted their control' 'with Qasr Ibrim occupied' (the page does not give the year of the recovery itself, so the revolt's year is used). Arqamani page (read in the repair pass): reign 'c. 215-205 BCE', 'Arqamani ruled in Meroë at the time of the Egyptian revolt of Horwennefer against Ptolemy IV Philopator' and 'his control above the reconquered Lower Nubia', with inscriptions 'from Kalabsha, Philae and the Temple of Dakka'; the earlier -200 sat outside that window. The earlier quotation 'taken back by the Kushite king ... Dodekaschoinos' was the Kush page's sentence about Yesebokheamani at the end of the 600 years (see the 298 event), not about this recovery. Open question: the Kush page has the northernmost part of Nubia 'occupied from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD' and the Dodekaschoinos page has Ptolemy VI renewing 'the incomes of the entire Dodekaschoinos' in 157 BC, so a Kushite hold of the Dodekaschoinos strip (about 4,000 km2, inside the gazetteer's Lower Nubia) between -204 and -22 is not settled by the pages (notes).

region.text: Lower Nubia between Aswan (Syene) and Napata: Petronius's invasion of 23 BC and the Kushite attack on Qasr Ibrim (Primis) in 22 BC

ledger.note: 23 BC: the Roman-Kushite war. 'In 23 BC, Publius Petronius invaded Nubia in response to a Nubian attack on southern Egypt'; 'In 22 BC, a large Kushite force moved northward with intention of attacking Qasr Ibrim' (Kush page); Rome had earlier 'drew the southern border of Roman Egypt at Aswan' after negotiations at Philae.

22 BC: peace between Rome and Meroë. Petronius 'sacked Napata in 22 BC'; 'A peace treaty between Rome and Meroë, under Augustus and Amanirenas, was signed in 22 BC' (the usual date of the Samos settlement, 21/20 BC, is on neither page).

region.text: the Dodekaschoinos: the border 'was moved to Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa)' and the arrangement 'guaranteed peace for most of the next 300 years'

ledger.note: 22 BC: the frontier fixed at Hiera Sykaminos. The Kush page does not date the border clause; the Meroë page dates the treaty 22 BC. Rome holds Philae to Maharraqa; Kush keeps Lower Nubia south of it (Qasr Ibrim).

region.text: the Dodekaschoinos to Philae: Yesebokheamani 'seems to have been the king who took control of the Dodecaschoenus after the Roman withdrawal in 298'

ledger.note: 298: Kush takes the Dodekaschoinos after Rome leaves it. Yesebokheamani page: 'He seems to have been the king who took control of the Dodecaschoenus after the Roman withdrawal in 298'; 'A monumental lion statue was erected at Qasr Ibrim in his honour'; reign 'approximate reign of 283-300' (Adams, cited). Dodekaschoinos page: the Romans 'abandoned the Dodekaschoinos in AD 298' and 'The Kushite king Yesebokheamani took control of the region and its defence against the Blemmyes'. Kush page: at the end of the 600-year occupation the territory 'was taken back by the Kushite king Yesebokheamani'. Earlier Kushite influence is not control: 'evidence of third century AD Kushite Kings at Philae in demotic and inscription' (Kush page); the Roman Dodekaschoinos 'was dominated by local Nubian priestly dynasties who acted as conduits of increasing Kushite influence' (Dodekaschoinos page). This replaces the earlier c. 250 gain (a researcher's midpoint) and the 297 loss to the Blemmyes: the Nobatia page ('invited into the region ... by the Roman Emperor Diocletian in 297 AD') and the Blemmyes page ('Peace with the Nobatae and Blemmyes moved Rome's southern border north to Philae') put the Nobatae and Blemmyes there, but the Dodekaschoinos and Yesebokheamani pages name Kush as the taker and name no Blemmye or Nobatian taking, and the Blemmyes' kingdom at Talmis is dated 'around 394', after Kush's end; the pages disagree and the dossier follows the three that name the taker. The roman-empire dossier (eu-04) should mirror the loss in 298.

region.text: Meroë, 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time' (Aksum page); Kush infobox 'Axumite capture of Meroë: 330'

ledger.note: 330: Aksum takes Meroë briefly. The pages disagree: Kush infobox 330; Kush text an expedition 'after 340' in which 'Ezana's army followed the course of the Atbara' and Meroë is not mentioned; Meroë page 'In 350 AD Meroë was destroyed by Axum' but 'the Aksumite presence was short-lived'; Ezana page: the Meroë stela may be Ezana's or Ousanas's and 'conclusive evidence ... is not currently available'. Hatched Aksumite occupation; the kingdom-of-axum dossier records the same event.

331: the Aksumites leave Meroë ('for a short period of time'; the end is undated, one year is the researcher's). Repair pass: the Ezana of Axum page (Ezana 'ruler of the Kingdom of Aksum (320s - c. 360 AD)') gives no year for a campaign at Meroë and says nothing of an Aksumite presence in Nubia afterwards; the end stays at one year.

region.text: Nubia from the first cataract to the Gezira: to Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia (Cliopatria 347), the Dodekaschoinos to the Blemmyes

ledger.note: Mid-4th century: Kush ends. 'the last pyramids as well as non-royal burials are dated to the mid-4th century, which is conventionally thought to be when the kingdom of Kush came to an end' (infobox 'Disestablished: c. 350 AD'); the Noba 'would not manage to break through until the 4th century'; 'Meroë was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia' (Meroë page). The year is Cliopatria's hand-over to its three Nubian rows.

wars.name: Kushite conquest of Egypt (Piye and Shabataka)

zones.text: Egypt from Thebes to the Delta

wars.outcome: Piye 'seized control of Lower Egypt around 727 BC' (campaigns 728-716 BC on the Victory Stela); Shabataka 'defeated the Saite kings of northern Egypt between 711 and 710 BC'; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty ruled Egypt from Memphis.
wars.note: The Twenty-fifth Dynasty page gives no conquest year; its table dates Piye c. 747-714 and Shebitku 714-705 and says Shebitku 'conquered the Nile Valley around 712 BC'.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory (infobox 'Assyrian victory', 'The Neo-Assyrian Empire vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years'): Memphis taken 671, retaken by Taharqa 669, lost 667; Tantamani's recovery after 664 ended at Memphis and Thebes in 663; Upper Egypt passed to Psamtik I in 656.
wars.note: Taharqa 'defeated the Assyrians outright in 674 BC' (Babylonian records; the raid itself 673). The Kush page says the war 'broke out' in 674.

wars.name: Psamtik II's Nubian campaign
wars.outcome: Napata sacked ('In 593 BC, it was sacked by the Egyptians'; Kush page: 'the sack of Napata by Psamtik II'); the capital moved to Meroë c. 591 BC. 'The last links between Kush and Upper Egypt were severed after hostilities with the Saite kings in the 590s BC'. No border is given.
wars.note: Empty zones: the pages name no land taken; the Napata page adds 'An Achaemenid raid had seriously affected Napata in 591 BC'.

wars.name: Ptolemy II's Nubian campaign

zones.text: the Triakontaschoinos, first to second cataract

wars.outcome: 'In 275 or 274 BC, Ptolemy II ... sent an army to Nubia, and defeated the Kingdom of Kush'; the Triakontaschoinos 'was annexed to Egypt'. The Dodekaschoinos 'was taken back by the Kushite king Yesebokheamani' after the Roman withdrawal of 298 (Yesebokheamani and Dodekaschoinos pages).

wars.name: Roman-Kushite war (Petronius)

zones.text: Lower Nubia: Syene, Philae, Qasr Ibrim (Primis)

wars.outcome: Petronius 'invaded Nubia in 23 BC' and 'sacked Napata in 22 BC'; the Kushites attacked Qasr Ibrim in 22 BC; a peace 'under Augustus and Amanirenas, was signed in 22 BC' (Meroë page) and the border 'was moved to Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa)', guaranteeing 'peace for most of the next 300 years' (Kush page).
wars.note: The war's start (the Kushite raid on Syene, 25/24 BC in the usual accounts) is undated on the pages; -25 is the researcher's. Napata page: Petronius 'invaded Kush with 10,000 men' in 23 BC.

wars.name: Aksumite campaigns against Meroë
wars.outcome: Aksum 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time' (Aksum page); an expedition 'after 340' followed the Atbara (Kush page); 'In 350 AD Meroë was destroyed by Axum' (Meroë page); the kingdom ended in the mid-4th century and Meroë 'was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia'.
wars.note: Three dates on four pages (330, after 340, 350); the ledger uses the infoboxes' 330 for the occupation and 346 for the end.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate; in Egypt (754-656 BC) the Kushite kings ruled through the existing nomes, so the Egyptian coast and desert edges follow Egypt's; the Nubian frontier with Ptolemaic Egypt after -274 is the second cataract, a reading of the Triakontaschoinos.
The Roman frontier at Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa) is a treaty line from 22 BC and is the one sharp border; the Butana, Bayuda and Red Sea Hills frontiers stay soft.

notes:
One state, not two. The brief asked whether Cliopatria's 1346-year row is successive states. The Kingdom of Kush page treats Napatan and Meroitic Kush as periods of one kingdom ('Following the severing of ties with Egypt, the Kushite imperial capital was located at Meroë'; 'In the Napatan Period ...', 'During the Meroitic period ...'), with Kerma as a separate earlier polity; the capital move of c. 591 BC is a capital_move event, not a new state. No split, no new slugs.

Start and end. Cliopatria -1000 sits between the page's 'around 1070 BC' independence, 'around 1000 BC' emergence and the infobox's 'c. 780 BC' (Alara 800-760 BC); kept, confidence 1. The end is Cliopatria's 346 (page: mid-4th century, infobox c. 350) so that Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia begin in 347 as Cliopatria has them.

Egypt. Cliopatria gives Kush all Egypt only for -700 to -676. The pages date Thebes to Kashta (c. 754, confidence 1; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty page doubts his control), Lower Egypt to Piye c. 727, the Saite Delta to 711-710, the losses to Esarhaddon 671, Ashurbanipal 667 and 663, and Upper Egypt to Psamtik I in 656. The me-02 (neo-assyrian-empire, assyrian-egypt) and me-03 (Egyptian dynasties) dossiers should carry the matching gains; Cliopatria's Twenty-second Dynasty row (-800 to -701) is the counterpart for the Kushite gains although the Theban and Saite rulers of the time were the Twenty-third and Twenty-fourth Dynasties, which Cliopatria lacks. Cliopatria's New Kingdom row (to -801) overlaps Kush in Nubia for 200 years.

Lower Nubia. The -630 to 337 shape always reaches 23.8 N. The pages give: Ptolemy II annexed the Triakontaschoinos in 275/274 BC; the Dodekaschoinos was 'taken back by the Kushite king' (undated; placed c. -200 at confidence 1); the Roman border at Hiera Sykaminos after the 22 BC peace; de facto Kushite control to Philae for part of the 3rd century AD (placed 250-297 at confidence 1); Diocletian's withdrawal to Philae in 297/298 handing the land to the Nobatae and Blemmyes. A gap-filler should open 'Dodekaschoinos', 'Triakontaschoinos' and 'Arqamani'. The gazetteer lacks Dodekaschoinos and Triakontaschoinos; the Dodekaschoinos is given as Lower Nubia within 115 km of Aswan.

Disagreements between pages: Aksum at Meroë 330 (Kush infobox, Aksum page), after 340 (Kush text), 350 (Meroë page), or not at all (Ezana page); the sack of Napata 593 BC (Napata page) or 'the 590s' (Kush page); the capital move 591 BC (Kush) or after 593 (Napata); Petronius 23 BC (Meroë, Napata) or the war of 22 BC (Kush); the Roman treaty 22 BC (Meroë page) against the usual 21/20 BC Samos date, which no page opened gives.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Blemmyes (blemmyes; Talmis/Kalabsha from c. 394, Lower Nubia in the late 4th-5th centuries; af-01-x), the Noba, Kerma (predecessor culture, 2450-1450 BC; af-01-x), Dʿmt. Rulers: no page opened gives a full dated king list (the Twenty-fifth Dynasty table covers 747-656 BC only), so the rulers key is omitted.

Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026), Egypt. The ledger no longer carries the Egyptian events of -754 to -656 (Kashta at Upper Egypt, Piye's Lower Egypt, Shabataka's Saite Delta, the contest, losses and gains against Assyria of -671 to -663, and Psamtik I at Thebes in -656). The Twenty-fifth Dynasty page treats Kush and Egypt under the dynasty as one realm ('a combined Nubian and Egyptian kingdom'; 'Kushite power stretched from the Mediterranean Sea to the present Ethiopian boundary'), but the dossiers split it into Nubia (this dossier) and Egypt (twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt, which dates Elephantine -754, Upper Egypt -728, the whole valley -712, the Assyrian contest -671 to -663 and the end in -656; hierarchy.csv makes it a constituent of Kush for -754 to -656). Drawing the same land twice made Kush take the Delta again at -669 while the dynasty's keyframe found it kept by others. The wars list keeps the campaigns as history.
